maya: Hey team — prepping Private deploy KMS plan. Quick Q: for envelope encryption in Private (VPC) should we use workload identity to let the runtime impersonate a cluster SA, or create a dedicated long-lived service account key?

raj: Definitely workload identity. No long-lived JSON keys if we can avoid it.

samir: +1. Workload identity + short-lived impersonation tokens. That keeps auditable principal and avoids key leakage risk.

maya: Good. For permissions, what IAM roles do we need on the key? I was thinking roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the runtime SA and roles/cloudkms.viewer for ops. Thoughts?

leo: That sounds right for encrypt/decrypt. Also give kms.viewer to security team for listings. For rotation we should avoid granting IAM on the key to too many people — use a separate key-admin SA for rotate ops.

raj: Example binding we used in staging:
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/private-kr/cryptoKeys/envelope-key \ 
  --member="serviceAccount:private-runtime@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \ 
  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
```

maya: Nice. How do we handle key rings per-customer vs per-cluster? Concerned about KMS quotas and approvals.

security-oncall: Recommend keyRing per-environment (prod/staging) and per-region if needed. Per-customer rings blow up management and IAM surface. Use envelope keys per-environment and include customer identifier in metadata for key access control at the application layer.

samir: Also consider using a per-tenant DEK stored in our DB encrypted with the same KEK (the KMS key). That keeps KMS ops simple and enables fast rotation of DEKs without touching KMS too often.

maya: Rotation cadence? monthly? quarterly?

security-oncall: For KEK rotate at least every 90 days for high-security customers, otherwise 180 days. But do automatic rotation with a rollover plan: create new key version, default-rotate, rewrap DEKs in background job, then retire old versions after N days.

raj: Operational notes: ensure Cloud Audit Logs for kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useCiphertext and cryptoKeyVersions.generateAccessToken are routed to our ELK/Stackdriver sinks. Flag any unexpected decrypt calls from new service accounts.

leo: Further: in Private deployments we sometimes run on customer-managed VPCs. If the control plane can't reach KMS (VPC-SC constraints), fallback policy = use local envelope cache for short grace period, but that requires approval. Add telemetry/gating.

maya: Who owns the rotation runbook and the rewrap job?

samir: Infra owns orchestration; security owns the policy and audit checks. I'll draft a runbook.

raj: Small gotcha — when using impersonation, gcloud iam service-accounts impersonate requires roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the caller SA. Make sure our private-controlplane SA has that on the runtime SA.

leo: Also prefer using the KMS symmetric keys for envelope (symmetric HOLD). We avoid asymmetric unless we need signing.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: New policy proposal uploaded: gs://redwood-secops/policies/private-kms-envelope-policy-v1.md

maya: Thanks — I'll pull that and comment. Action items:
- raj: add workload-identity example and gcloud snippets to infra repo (due EOD).
- samir: draft rotation runbook (eta 2d).
- leo: wire audit log sink alerts for unexpected decrypt ops (eta 1d).

raj: acked.

security-oncall: If anyone wants to test rewrap flow, ping me and I'll give a short window on staging key to practice. :lock:

maya: Perfect. Closing for now — will post PR for policy changes. :sparkles:
